summary: IdP metadata with multiple EntityDescriptor entries and trailing-slash EntityID causes partner selection misroute and service token 401s in private
description: Issue summary: After Brightline Health rotated their IdP metadata feed, a metadata document containing multiple EntityDescriptor elements (federated tenants) started causing service-account token exchanges to fail. Impact: Scheduled batch workers and some admin APIs returned 401/403 for service-to-service calls. This was observed only in Brightline's private deployment (VPC) after the rotation. The symptom appears to be misselection of the IdP EntityDescriptor entry when EntityID variants exist (one with trailing slash, one without), causing JWKS and signing-key lookups to hit the wrong metadata and therefore failing signature validation during token exchange.
impact: Several scheduled batch workers failed their daily runs (30-40% of jobs), customer-facing admin operations intermittently blocked; engineering and ops are blocked from performing tenant-scoped admin actions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In a private deployment, upload IdP metadata XML that contains two EntityDescriptor elements for the same logical partner with slightly different entityID values (e.g., https://idp.example.com/ and https://idp.example.com).
2) Trigger a service token exchange or SAML assertion validation flow for a scheduled worker.
3) Observe 401/403 during token validation and mismatched JWKS/key URLs being fetched.
4) Replacing the metadata with a single canonical EntityDescriptor resolves the failures.
logs:
2026-03-08T03:12:42Z auth: token-exchange error: signature_verification_failed (issuer=https://idp.example.com, resolved_entityid=https://idp.example.com/ )
2026-03-08T03:12:42Z identity-proxy: fetched jwks from https://idp-wrong.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json (status 200) but kid mismatch
Brightline-proxy logs show metadata parsing: matched entity by prefix, selected EntityDescriptor index 2 (entityID endswith '/'), canonicalization step didn't normalize trailing slash
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in staging by creating a two-EntityDescriptor metadata file.
- Parser currently performs a string equality or prefix match on entityID rather than normalized URI comparison. Trailing slash variants can cause the selection logic to prefer the second descriptor.
- Observed that our metadata cache key uses the raw entityID string; metadata refresh uses the first matching descriptor from the XML parsing library.
- Customer rotated metadata at 2026-03-07 23:45 UTC; failures began at first token exchange after cache refresh.
- No evidence of network issues or proxy rewriting; the wrong JWKS URL came directly from the non-canonical EntityDescriptor selected by parser.
comments: 2026-03-08 - Support (Ava Rodriguez): Customer reported mass job failures after IdP rotation. Collected metadata XML and logs. Escalated to SRE and Auth team.
2026-03-09 - SRE (Rohan Iyer): Confirmed reproduction in our staging. Parser logic noted. Created internal ticket INT-76321 for parser fix and cache migration.

2026-03-10 - Eng (Priya Menon): Hypothesis: normalize entityID URIs (parse and compare host+path normalization) and prefer exact match without trailing slash; fallback to other descriptors with explicit log. Preparing PR.

2026-03-11 - Support (Ava Rodriguez): Shared mitigation steps with customer: temporarily provide single-EntityDescriptor metadata or canonicalize entityID on upload. Customer applied single entry and reported jobs recovered.

2026-03-12 - Eng (Rohan Iyer): Submitted PR to change selection to normalized-URI matching and to add a debug field in metadata cache entries (see PR 1284). Planning staged rollout to private control plane tomorrow.

2026-03-13 - Customer (Brightline Health - Lisa Tran): Confirmed that after temporary metadata change, scheduled workers retried successfully. Asked for permanent fix timeline and request for postmortem.
2026-03-13 - Support (Ava Rodriguez): Noted follow-up to schedule postmortem and coordinate fix deployment window with customer maintenance hours.
2026-03-13 - Eng (Rohan Iyer): Rolling change will include migration that rekeys metadata cache by normalized_entityid and emits a warning when multiple EntityDescriptor entries are detected.
root_cause: Metadata selection logic used raw string matching and returned a non-canonical EntityDescriptor when multiple entries existed. Trailing-slash differences in entityID produced an incorrect JWKS/signing-key selection, causing signature validation failures during token exchange.
resolution:
Workaround: Customer replaced metadata with a single canonical EntityDescriptor (immediate).
Permanent fix: Eng merged PR to normalize entityID URIs during metadata parse and to update metadata cache keys; rollout scheduled to private control planes 2026-03-16 during low-traffic window. Added detection to flag multi-EntityDescriptor metadata at upload and a recommended remediation message in Console.
resolution_notes:
- PR merged: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1284
- Private control plane rollout scheduled 2026-03-16 02:00-03:00 UTC for us-east customers.
- Post-deployment, we will run metadata rekey job to normalize cache entries for affected customers and notify Brightline Health when complete.
- Follow-up action: add automated metadata validation at upload to warn about multiple EntityDescriptors and entityID normalization suggestions.
next_steps:
1) Coordinate with Brightline Health for scheduled rollout confirmation and notify about expected 5-10 minute control plane restart.
2) After rollout, run cache migration job and validate successful token exchanges.
3) Publish short postmortem and update Console upload validation UX.
4) Backfill unit tests for metadata parsing edge cases.
time_to_restore: 6 hours (customer applied workaround; full platform fix pending rollout)
customer_communication: Support provided immediate workaround and status updates. Customer accepted workaround and requested timeline for permanent fix. Will be notified once rollout completes and when cache migration runs.
